chunks: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام:
About hides and furs that a man purchases in a market from the markets of al-Jabal: should he ask about its proper slaughter if the seller is a Muslim who is not an ʿārif?
He عليه السلام said: “You must ask about it if you see the polytheists selling that. But if you see them performing salat, then do not ask about it.”

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: polytheists, whose sale raises the need for inquiry
key_terms.ذَكَاتِهِ: its lawful slaughter and purification for use
key_terms.غَيْرَ عَارِفٍ: not recognized as an adherent with correct doctrinal recognition
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: a Muslim, whose outward Islam affects the ruling
key_terms.يُصَلُّونَ: they perform salat, indicating outward Islam

ai.seo_question: When must one ask about the slaughter status of leather and fur bought in the market?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about purchasing leather and fur items and whether one must investigate their proper slaughter. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between cases that raise doubt, such as when polytheists are seen selling them, and cases where the outward sign of Islam, namely salat, removes the need for inquiry.
